approved: Civil Aviation Amendment (Unmanned Aircraft Levy Collection and Payment) Bill 2020
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would create a levy on commercial and professional users of remotely piloted aircraft to recover the costs of regulation and registration.
It would amend the Civil Aviation Act 1998 to allow the Civil Aviation Safety Authority to collect the levy and require the Commonwealth to pay those amounts to CASA.
The levy amount would be set by regulations and cannot exceed $300, and the scheme would start on 30 September 2020.
Amends the Civil Aviation Act 1998 to establish arrangements for CASA to collect the unmanned aircraft levy.
Inserts a new section 46A requiring the Commonwealth to pay CASA amounts equal to the levy received.
Appropriates the Consolidated Revenue Fund for those payments.
Commercial and professional users of remotely piloted aircraft and model aircraft operators.

Two bills were introduced to establish a cost-recovery levy on commercial remotely piloted aircraft (drone) operators to fund the Civil Aviation Safety Authority’s regulatory functions, with no levy set for the current financial year.

The Civil Aviation Amendment (Unmanned Aircraft Levy Collection and Payment) Bill 2020 establishes a mechanism for the Commonwealth to pay the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) the levy amounts collected from remotely piloted aircraft operators, supporting long-term safe and lawful operations.

The opposition supports the drone levy bills but will move an amendment, citing concerns that registration fees of up to $300 are far higher than comparable fees of $16 in the UK, $7 in the US and $5 in Canada. The speaker also criticised the government for failing to support the broader aviation sector during COVID-19, noting 3,000 job losses at Virgin, 5,000 at Dnata and 8,500 at Qantas, and called for a sector-wide aviation recovery plan.

The bills enable CASA to continue regulating remotely piloted aircraft (drones) through a cost-recovery levy on commercial operators, with registration starting 30 September 2020 but no fees until mid-2021; recreational users are exempt.
